tabs.title: Who she is
tabs.description: Getting to know Divya Raghavan (32, staff engineer at a US-headquartered product company) — buying a 2BHK in JP Nagar–Bannerghatta Road near the Yellow Line metro stretch, entirely in her own name, with a checklist tuned for single-woman ownership and a security culture she verifies at 11 pm.

buyers.name: Divya Raghavan
buyers.description: Ten years, six flats, three kinds of landlord indignity — radicalized by a broker who asked her to bring her father on a video call. Now buys with her own signature: solo EMI, solo deed, solo door. Audits communities at 11 pm and 6 am, and quietly tracks which security desks log women's guests with a smirk.

tabs.sharedVisionDescription: Convert a decade of six rented flats and three kinds of landlord indignity into a Yellow Line 2BHK carrying one name on the deed — her own. A gated community with real security, not surveillance; an RWA sociable but boundaried; cafes and a gym walkable; security she can verify at 11 pm; a balcony for the plant ambitions; and a flat she can lock and travel from for three weeks — a settlement with the city that treated her as temporary.

chatMessages.text: Riya, honest opinion time. The beige 2BHK — sensible, east-facing, resells in a weekend. The top-floor one has that terrace… aiyyo, that terrace, pa.
Don't waste the coffee. Here's my only question — what is each flat FOR? Not for anyone's future seller. For you, at eleven pm, with the logbook open.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Divya's diligence instrument was time-of-day. Any community can host a polite sales tour at 11 am; very few survive an 11 pm visit with the logbook open and the tea steaming. She built a second checklist — security culture, guest-logging norms, single-women owner density — that exists nowhere on any portal, and it failed two glossy projects that every price sheet in Bengaluru would have called premium. When the beige-versus-terrace question came, she answered it the same way she'd audited the desks: what is each flat FOR? The beige one funds the actual life. The rest is just square feet.”

lessons.title: The unwritten checklist matters more than the portal's.
lessons.description: Security culture, single-women owner density, guest-logging norms — none of it exists online. She built it by visiting at 11 pm and 6 am and asking women residents directly. Two glossy projects failed it.

differentlyCards.title: Start the 11 pm audits earlier
differentlyCards.description: Two glossy communities ate a month of shortlisting — the time-of-day test should have been gate one, not gate three.

differentlyCards.title: Talk to the lawyer before shortlisting
differentlyCards.description: Nomination and will questions would have shaped the unit choice itself — thirty lawyer-minutes could have been spent earlier.

differentlyCards.title: File every broker chat, from day one
differentlyCards.description: The 'father on video call' screenshot radicalised her in month one; earlier filing would have flagged the pattern sooner.

differentlyCards.title: Ask the 'co-applicant' question up front
differentlyCards.description: Adding one question to the first call — 'do you require a co-applicant for solo women buyers?' — would have cut two office visits.

chatMessages.text: One name on the deed, a Yellow Line walk, and a balcony that now has sixty pots. I think I finally stopped being a tenant of Bengaluru.
You stopped being a tenant the week you filed that broker chat. The deed just caught up with the decision.
